sources.title: Mahābhārata, Book 2 (Sabhāparvan), Section V: Nārada enters the assembly
sources.edition: Kisari Mohan Ganguli, trans., The Mahabharata of Krishna-Dwaipayana Vyasa, Book 2: Sabha Parva (1883–1896), digitized text in the Internet Sacred Text Archive; sectional labels and printed page numbers follow this edition.

notes: Scope: Sabha Parva §§IV–V. Section IV’s named sages and Kṣatriyas are recorded as attending Yudhiṣṭhira’s assembly; §V adds Nārada’s four named companions and reception. Section VI is omitted because it is a prelude to the celestial assembly descriptions in §§VII–XI and adds no new roster beyond this batch’s §V.

Previously defined same-figure nodes reused rather than duplicated: Asita, Devala, Mārkaṇḍeya, Bhṛgu, Parvata, Gālava, Pavitrapāṇi, Bhāluki, Yājñavalkya, Pārāśarya, Kakṣīvat, Gautama, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Marīci, Nārada, Tumburu. Section IV’s Chittasena is source-scoped separately from the similarly named §X Citraseṇa because the passage does not explicitly link them. These IDs are defined in the prior mb_sabha_people.json or mb_sabha_earlier.json batches.

Only individually named persons who attend the assembly or have a direct stated relation are included. Arjuna is mentioned as teacher of the unnamed princes but is not claimed as an attendee.  Unnamed Brahmanas, the unnamed son of Śiśupāla, the unnamed son of Lomaharṣaṇa, unnamed kings/rulers of regions, generic Kṣatriya and Gandharva groups, and princes described only as disciples are excluded.

Namesakes remain source-scoped: sage and Kṣatriya Sumitra; sage Vali vs. Asura-list Vali; Kunti as male Kṣatriya vs. Pṛthā/Kuntī; Sātyaka vs. Sātyaki; two Naciketa roster mentions; Sunaka is one person despite repetition; Aniruddha and Śaivya are each one local referent despite repeated mention.

Parentage claims are restricted to the translation’s explicit statements: Rukmiṇī→Pradyumna, Śini→Sātyaka, and Satyaki→Yuyudhāna as Ganguli renders it. This preserves a potentially variant or problematic Satyaki/Sātyaka distinction instead of merging it.
Count: 112 newly defined person nodes, 18 reused person anchors, and 132 explicit attendance/relationship claims.
